name: RDE 1
label: RDE
tooltip: Rotating disk electrode. Supports RRDE configuration.
overview:
The Autolab RDE is a high-end rotating disk electrode designed for measurements on systems requiring high rotation speeds and low noise levels. This unit can reach speeds of up to 10,000 rpm, and a liquid mercury contact ensures low-noise operation. The PCTFE shaft has been designed to fit both Metrohm cell vessels and most other electrochemical cells. The tip diameter is 10 mm, with an active surface diameter of either 3 or 5 mm.

The RDE rotation speed is manually controlled using the knob located on the front panel of the motor control unit. The RDE can also be remotely controlled via Autolab software. The rotation speed can be continuously adjusted from 100 to 10,000 rpm, with a resolution of 1 rpm.
specs: High-performance rotating disk electrode designed for electrochemical measurements under controlled hydrodynamic conditions
High-speed operation up to 10,000 rpm with continuous rotation control from 100 to 10,000 rpm (1 rpm resolution)
Low-noise measurements enabled by a sealed liquid mercury contact
Compatible with Metrohm cells and most standard electrochemical cells thanks to the PCTFE shaft design
Interchangeable electrode tips with 3 mm or 5 mm active surface areas (Pt, Au, Ag, and glassy carbon options)
Manual or software-controlled rotation speed via Autolab control software

name: AFM-SECM
desc: Icon FastScan with MB20G Glovebox System and an Acoustic Hood The AVH-1000
label: Microscopy
tooltip: Atomic Force Microscope for surface topography at sub-nanometre resolution. Contact and tapping modes available. A three-gloves glove-box allows a controlled atmosphere. Accoustic Hood is also available to accurate measurements in ambiant atmosphere.
overview:
The Bruker Dimension FastScan® Atomic Force Microscope (AFM) is a high-performance nanoscale characterization platform designed to achieve high-speed imaging without compromising resolution, force control, or measurement accuracy. It enables real-time visualization of dynamic nanoscale phenomena in both air and liquid environments, making it particularly suitable for advanced materials characterization, surface science, electrochemistry, and interface studies.

The system combines exceptional imaging speed with high-resolution topographical and physicochemical mapping capabilities, allowing researchers to rapidly explore large sample areas while maintaining nanoscale and sub-nanometer sensitivity. The FastScan technology enables scan rates significantly higher than conventional AFM systems, with optimized feedback control for stable imaging of complex and dynamic surfaces.

Equipped with advanced AFM modes, including PeakForce Tapping®, nanomechanical mapping, force spectroscopy, electrical characterization, and surface property analysis, the instrument provides simultaneous access to topographical, mechanical, electrical, and adhesion information at the nanoscale. It is therefore highly relevant for the investigation of catalysts, electrode materials, polymers, thin films, and functional interfaces.

The microscope includes a controlled acoustic enclosure (acoustic hood) to minimize external noise disturbances and improve measurement stability, enabling high-quality AFM imaging under demanding experimental conditions. The system is also integrated with a glove box environment, allowing the characterization of air-sensitive, moisture-sensitive, or chemically reactive samples under controlled atmosphere conditions.

Thanks to its combination of high-speed imaging, advanced nanoscale characterization modes, environmental control, and low-noise operation, the Bruker Dimension FastScan AFM represents a unique tool for studying solid–liquid interfaces, electrochemical materials, catalytic surfaces, and next-generation energy materials.
specs: High-speed Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) platform for nanoscale surface characterization
High-resolution imaging with fast scanning capabilities for dynamic and complex samples
Advanced AFM modes including PeakForce Tapping®, force spectroscopy, and nanomechanical mapping
Nanoscale characterization of surface morphology, mechanical properties, adhesion, and material heterogeneity

Suitable for sensitive materials, electrochemical interfaces, catalysts, polymers, thin films, and energy-related materials
High-precision positioning and optimized feedback control for stable nanoscale imaging
Compatible with advanced studies of solid–liquid interfaces and electrochemical materials

name: DEMS
label: Differential Electrochemical Mass Spectrometer
tooltip: Differential Electrochemical Mass Spectrometer for real-time detection of gaseous products during electrochemical reactions.
overview:
The LIQUIDLOOP DEMS (Differential Electrochemical Mass Spectrometry) system is an advanced analytical platform designed for real-time investigation of electrochemical reaction mechanisms.
It combines electrochemical control with high-sensitivity mass spectrometric detection, enabling the direct monitoring of gaseous and volatile reaction intermediates during electrochemical processes.
The system is based on a modular architecture integrating a FlowSys 2.0 gas–electrolyte flow management unit, a PoGASi DEMS interface with an integrated vacuum stage, an electrochemical capillary cell, and a mass spectrometer for rapid product identification.
This configuration allows researchers to correlate electrochemical signals, such as current variations and potential changes, with the formation of specific reaction products in real time.
The LIQUIDLOOP DEMS platform is particularly suited for studying complex electrocatalytic reactions, including CO₂ reduction, nitrogen reduction, oxygen evolution, and organic electrosynthesis pathways.
By minimizing transport limitations between the electrochemical interface and the mass spectrometer, the system provides high temporal resolution and improved sensitivity compared with conventional offline analytical techniques.
Its flexible design supports different electrode materials, electrolyte conditions, and experimental configurations, making it suitable for fundamental research as well as catalyst development.
The integration of controlled liquid flow, vacuum coupling, and precise mass analysis enables detailed mechanistic studies of reaction intermediates and catalytic selectivity.
The DEMS approach provided by LIQUIDLOOP helps researchers optimize next-generation energy conversion technologies by linking material properties with real operating conditions.
